tagline: A season with the players below the stars.

opener: A new season at the old barn. Same boards, same hopes.
First game of the year. Nobody has lost one yet.
The ice is in and the {team} are back. That is enough for tonight.
Opening night. Half the town is here and the other half has the radio on.
Another season. The club is still open, which was not a sure thing.
winStreak: {n} wins in a row for the {team}. Nobody is saying it out loud yet.
That is {n} straight. The {town} barn has not been this loud in a while.
{n} in a row. The room is quiet about it, which is the right way to be.
The {team} have won {n} straight and still dress the same six.
{n} wins running. Somebody check the standings twice.
loseStreak: {n} losses in a row. The {team} will dress tonight all the same.
That is {n} straight the wrong way. Nobody quits on a {town} winter.
{n} in a row dropped. The club has seen worse and stayed open.
A hard stretch: {n} straight losses. The answer is the next shift.
{n} losses running. The coffee at the rink is still hot.
lastStrike: One more loss and the season is over. The {team} know it.
No room left: the next loss ends it. Skate accordingly.
The {team} are down to their last strike. Everybody in {town} can count.
Lose tonight and the lights go off until autumn.
Last strike. It has to be tonight and every night after.
rival: The {rival} again. These two do not need an introduction.
{rival} tonight. Nobody in {town} needs the schedule to know that.
Another night with the {rival}. Bring a second stick.
The {team} and the {rival}. It was never going to be a quiet one.
It is the {rival}. Some games mean more and this is one.
boss: {boss} tonight. {person}, their {role}, has seen clubs like this come and go.
The {team} against {boss}. {person} will have them ready.
{boss}, and {person} with them. A long night's work ahead.
Nobody gave the {team} this game. That has not stopped them before.
{boss} are the measure. {person} is the reason.
broke: Money is tight at the {team}. The club plays tonight; next month is another matter.
The treasurer is not sleeping. The {team} skate anyway.
There is talk about the books. A full barn would help.
The club is short and everybody knows it. Buy a program.
Lean times for the {team}. They have kept the doors open before.
playoffs: Playoff hockey in {town}. The beards are coming in.
This is what the long winter was for.
The {team} are in. From here every night could be the last one.
Playoffs. The whole season comes down to a few shifts.
Nobody expected the {team} here in October. Here they are.
champions: The banner went up over the summer. Now everyone wants to take it down.
Champions a year ago. That buys nothing tonight.
The {team} raised a banner. The league has not forgotten.
Defending the title. It is harder to keep than to win.
Last year's champions dress tonight. Same room, new target on it.
veteran: {player} is {age} and still first on the ice for warm-up.
Another night for {player}. At {age} he counts them.
{player}, {age}, in the lineup. He has forgotten more than most learn.
At {age}, {player} is still here. So is the club.
rookie: {player} is {age} and playing like he has somewhere to be.
Keep an eye on {player}. {age} years old and already on the sheet.
The kid, {player}, has {goals} this season. Nobody wanted him either.
{player}, {age}, is finding his feet. The room has taken to him.
A {age}-year-old named {player} is turning into something.
hot: {player} has {goals} this season and wants more.
{goals} goals for {player}. He was on waivers a year ago.
{player} leads the {team} with {goals}. He would tell you it is the linemates.
{player}, {goals} on the year. The third line is paying its way.
plain: Another night at the rink. The {team} dress six and a goalie, same as always.
A regular night in {town}. Those count too.
The {team} are at it again. Nothing fancy.
Two points on the table and a cold night outside.
Hockey tonight. The club is open and the ice is good.
The {team} skate tonight. That is the whole story so far.
